name: TPG World Championship
epitaph: The belt the fed's own commentary said had returned to The Proving Grounds when Kris Adams won it at Madison Square Garden on 17 December 2005, beating JC Sinn with a frog splash thrown as a tribute. Before that the record is thin and out of order: PWE's own roster records name Chris Watts a former TPG World Champion without a date, and the chairman who had it carried to the ring that night, Mikel Sweeten, is never called champion in words. The fed billed the same belt as its Heavyweight Championship in the weeks either side.
notes: Sources disagree on who held it going into End of an Era III: the show's own announcer crowns a NEW World Champion, and the show's own staging has Mikel Sweeten walk out with the belt over his shoulder without ever being introduced as its holder. Both readings are recorded; no reign is written for Sweeten. An unresolved claim sits between this belt and the other: FoB's own Rebirth of 20 September 2005 has its commentary announce an interfering wrestler as “THAT'S MORTIS! THE TPG CHAMPION!!” (FoB's own Rebirth of 20 September 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-rebirth-2005-09-20-9684.html)), and the fed's own record names no belt he could have been carrying. Both of this promotion's singles championships are candidates and no document names one; the claim is recorded on both rows and settled on neither. The fed's own booking blurb of 10 December 2005 calls it “the returning 'TPG Heavyweight Championship'” a week before it was won (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/standard-match-2005-12-10.html).

name: TPG International Championship
epitaph: The fed's own second belt and, by its own commentary, the one both of its last two champions won out of a tournament — each of them going through David D to get there. Wil the Thrill retained it in a main event against Carlito Caribbean Cool in the spring of 2005; Edge held it after him; JC Sinn carried it into December. On 9 October 2005 the fed ran three first-round matches for it in one night, and its founder came back at Christmas to demand it be dropped for the Pride Title instead.
notes: No title history survives: the pinned TPG: Title History thread is listed on the fed's own roleplay forum, posted 4 December 2005, and was never captured (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/forum-tpg-aggression-132.html). An unresolved claim sits between this belt and the other: FoB's own Rebirth of 20 September 2005 has its commentary announce an interfering wrestler as “THAT'S MORTIS! THE TPG CHAMPION!!” (FoB's own Rebirth of 20 September 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-rebirth-2005-09-20-9684.html)), and the fed's own record names no belt he could have been carrying. Both of this promotion's singles championships are candidates and no document names one; the claim is recorded on both rows and settled on neither.

name: TPG Diva Championship
epitaph: Held by Trish Stratus for as long as the belt had existed, in the fed's own commentary's words, and lost in three minutes and fifty-seven seconds to a flapjack slam from So Cal Val at Madison Square Garden on 17 December 2005. Two months earlier its champion had stood in the ring and demanded a match putting both of the fed's women's titles on the line at once.
notes: The fed staged two women's champions at the same time — this belt and a Women's Championship held by Lacey — and its own segment calls them collectively “both TPG Diva Titles” (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-uncensored-results-2005-10-10.html).

name: TPG Women's Championship
epitaph: Introduced on 9 October 2005 with its champion, Lacey, showing it off to a crowd chanting that she sucked. The fed's own commentary calls her “one of two women's champions”, and its own segment that night has the other one demand a match to put both belts on the line. Nothing in the record says whether that match happened.
notes: Named only by the ring announcer's introduction and the commentary around it (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-uncensored-results-2005-10-10.html); no other document in the held record mentions the belt.

name: TPG Pride Title
epitaph: AJ Styles held it seventy-nine days and was still arguing about it in August 2004, by which point the fed had taken it away — “the TPG Pride Title is dead now,” one of his own opponents told him, “demolished; taken away.” Sixteen months later the fed's founder came back to Madison Square Garden asking why an International Championship was being paraded around with the Pride Title sitting on the sidelines, and the chairman offered to burn the International belt in front of him and bring this one back instead. It came back: the last line the record ever writes about the promotion has Montel Vontavious Porter defending it in May 2007.

events.note: The fed's own roleplay text of August 2004 has the belt already gone — “Only the Pride Title has been demolished; taken away” — with no date and no closing match recorded. It was defended again by 2007, so the event records what happened, not a permanent state.

notes: Both the reign and the retirement come from one served document: AJ Styles's own signature record and the promo exchange around it (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/iron-man-battle-royal-2004-08-16.html). The board's own last capture, of 27 May 2007, carries a news line reading “TPG Showcase: Pride Title: Montel Vontavious Porter © d. The Mask”, which is held in the workshop and not served and is registered here as a second reign. The belt the fed's own chairman offered to bring back at Madison Square Garden in December 2005 was defended again, under the same name, eighteen months later.

name: TPG Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Randy Walker walked out of The Proving Grounds still holding it and onto PWE Underground, where he told a camera that being hardcore champion was what had held him back and offered the belt to anyone who had a use for it. That is the whole of the record.

name: TPG Tag Team Championship
aka: TPG Inter promotional Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The Patriots — Joey Legend and Daniel Justice — are the only champions the record names, and it names them in the past tense, in a news line about a match they were losing somewhere else.

name: TPG North American Championship
epitaph: Named once, in a member's own reply to a December 2005 roleplay thread endorsing a contender for it. No champion, no match and no other mention of the belt survives.
notes: The sole receipt is one line in the fed's own Aggression roleplay thread of 9 December 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/kick-in-the-door-wavin-the-four-four-2005-12-09.html). A second, in-fiction mention survives beside it: David D's own manager asks in a roleplay of 11 December 2005 “why would you want to just champion of North America when you can be the intercontinental champion”, and John Bradshaw Layfield's roleplay of the same week lists “North American Champion, International Champion, and especially The Proving Ground's Heavyweight Championship” as the three belts his opponent might chase (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/1-in-cont-s-match-2005-12-10.html; /promotions/pwe-inc/archive/standard-match-2005-12-10.html).
